message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to cancel a date because I'm really tired. Let me start by understanding the situation better. I've been talking to this guy for two weeks, and we had our first date a week after we started talking. That went well, and then we had our second date on Wednesday. Now it's Friday in Australia, and we were supposed to have our third date tonight to watch a movie. On the second date, I mentioned that some things she said over the last week had been a bit overwhelming because she was planning too far ahead. I just wanted to be honest and let her know that I wanted to take things slow, and she understood. We made plans to hang out on Friday night to watch a movie. This week has been really long for me. I've had a ridiculously long week with only about four hours of sleep and worked from 7 am to 5 pm with only a half-hour break. I was really exhausted. When he asked me around 5:30 pm if we were grabbing dinner or if he should get something himself, I told him I felt horrible but I was absolutely shattered and would probably just fall asleep. I asked if we could do it on Sunday instead, and I said I'd take him out to lunch and pay, and we could watch a movie. I haven't received a response from him yet. Now I'm worried that after him thinking I wanted out of the relationship, plus now canceling the date, he might think I'm not interested anymore. Is it AITA (Are We In Trouble) for rescheduling a date when he already has doubts about me? Alright, so I need to think about whether canceling the date because I'm tired is right or wrong. Let's break this down. First, communication is key in any relationship. I was honest with him about feeling overwhelmed and wanting to take things slow. That's good because it shows transparency and respect for his feelings. However, when I canceled the date, I might have come across as dismissive or uninterested, especially if he already had doubts about me. On the other hand, taking care of my well-being is important too. If I'm exhausted, forcing myself to go on a date might not be fair to either of us. It's better to reschedule when I'm in a better state of mind. But I need to communicate this in a way that reassures him that I'm still interested and that it's just about my current situation. Maybe I should have explained my reasons more clearly and reassured him that I want to see him, but I need a little more time to rest. That way, he knows it's not about him but about my well-being. I also need to consider how he might perceive this. If he's already had doubts, canceling the date without a clear explanation might reinforce those doubts. It's important to address his concerns and ensure he understands that this is a temporary situation and not a reflection of my interest in him. In summary, while it's important to take care of myself, I also need to communicate my reasons clearly and reassure him of my interest. Otherwise, canceling the date might be seen as AITA, especially if he already has doubts about the relationship.
